Ukraine aid row: EU withholds $1.7 billion; Zelenskyy's new bill faces internal and external pressure
item.description: The European Union has frozen $1.7 billion in aid to Ukraine following concerns over a new law perceived to weaken anti-corruption agencies. This decision, impacting over a third of the EU's Ukraine Facility fund, stems from the legislation granting the Prosecutor General greater control over anti-corruption bodies.

item.title: Cincinnati shocker: Man stomped, woman knocked out in brawl; crowd jeers and films
item.description: A shocking video from Cincinnati shows a man and woman violently attacked during a downtown brawl. The man was chased, beaten, and stomped on, while the woman was punched unconscious when she tried to help. Police are investigating the incident, sparked by a possible exchange of racial slurs.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In just six months, Dubai’s transport system carried more people than the entire US population
item.description: Dubai recorded 395.3 million public transport rides in H1 2025, 35 times its population, driven by metro, buses, taxis, and shared mobility. This marks a 9% year-on-year rise. Major expansions like the Dubai Metro Blue Line and a fleet of 637 low-emission-buses are underway, reinforcing Dubai’s long-term goal of sustainable, accessible, and integrated transport for all.

MAGA singer’s Canada gigs cancelled: Backlash over Sean Feucht’s anti-diversity views
item.description: Parks Canada cancelled Sean Feucht's concert permit at York Redoubt due to safety concerns arising from his controversial social media posts regarding 2SLGBTQ+ rights, women's rights, and diversity. Despite permit revocations in multiple locations, Feucht performed at a private venue in Nova Scotia, hosted by pastors who faced backlash for supporting his event. Feucht responded by claiming religious discrimination.

item.title: Harry and the Diary of Reconciliation: Prince to share calendar with palace to avoid clashes
item.description: Prince Harry has agreed to share his schedule with the royal family to prevent public appearance clashes, especially after his Angola trip overshadowed Queen Camilla's birthday. He aims to ease tensions and is seeking a personal reconnection with King Charles, who remains cautious. Harry fears being permanently excluded by Prince William in the future.

item.title: Hero bystanders stopped Walmart stabber: Derrick Perry held attacker at gunpoint; praised online
item.description: A stabbing attack at a Traverse City Walmart injured 11 people before bystanders intervened. Derrick Perry, identified by family and locals, is being hailed as a hero for drawing his licensed weapon and holding the suspect, Bradford James Gille, at gunpoint. Perry, along with a former Marine who used a shopping cart, stopped Gille until police arrived, preventing further harm.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Did Epstein introduce Melania to Trump? Biographer makes bold claim; first lady's says otherwise
item.description: Michael Wolff has stirred controversy by alleging Jeffrey Epstein played a role in introducing Melania Trump to Donald Trump. Wolff claims Melania was involved in Epstein's social circle and connected through Paolo Zampolli. Melania denies this, saying she met Trump at the Kit Kat Klub. Despite Trump's attempts to distance himself, photos and Epstein's claims suggest otherwise.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tom Lehrer dies at 97: Satirical singer found dead at home; famed for taboo-breaking songs
item.description: American satirist Tom Lehrer passed away at 97. He was famous for his darkly comic songs. Lehrer gained recognition in the 1950s and 60s. He was also a mathematician who taught at prestigious universities. His satirical songs tackled war, drug use, and religion. Lehrer's work remained popular through radio and stage shows. He never married and had no children.

item.title: What is Golf Force One? Trump's armoured buggy patrols Scottish golf course
item.description: Donald Trump visited his golf course in South Ayrshire, Scotland. Security was tight, including an armored golf cart. Protests occurred in Edinburgh and other UK cities during the visit. Demonstrators voiced opposition to Trump's politics. One protester breached security at the golf course. Trump played golf with his son Eric and ambassador Warren Stephens despite the demonstrations.

item.title: Second airport backed by Abu Dhabi inaugurated in the Maldives with AED 330.5 million investment
item.description: The Maldives today inaugurated the upgraded Velana International Airport, supported by Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD) and regional partners, boosting capacity to over 7 million passengers annually. This inauguration follows the recent opening of Maafaru International Airport. Together, these projects enhance the nation’s connectivity and tourism growth, reflecting ADFD’s enduring commitment to sustainable development and economic progress in the Maldives.
